Which of the following is one of Markowi.Investors can borrow and lend unlimited: Unlimited borrowing/lending at the risk-free rate is a CAPM assumption added later by Sharpe, not part of Markowitz's list.
Which of the following is one of Markowi.Investors measure portfolio risk with be: MPT measures risk with standard deviation; beta is the CAPM/SML risk measure.
Which of the following is one of Markowi.Investor indifference strengthens the fu: MPT assumes indifference diminishes beyond the holding period, not that it strengthens.

Based on these facts, which conclusion i.The current portfolio is efficient becau: Being attainable is not the same as efficient; the current portfolio earns less than the frontier offers at 12% risk.
Based on these facts, which conclusion i.The proposed portfolio dominates and sho: A 10% return at 12% risk lies above the frontier, so it cannot be constructed from this asset universe.
Based on these facts, which conclusion i.Both portfolios are efficient because th: Equal risk does not make portfolios efficient; only the frontier point (8%) is efficient at that risk.

Compared with a moderately risk-tolerant.flatter, touching the efficient frontier: Flat curves belong to risk-tolerant investors, not risk-averse ones.
Compared with a moderately risk-tolerant.steeper, touching the efficient frontier: Steep curves produce a tangency to the left (lower risk), not to the right.
Compared with a moderately risk-tolerant.downward sloping, since added risk lower: Indifference curves slope upward because more risk requires more return.

Investor A's indifference curve is tange.B has steeper indifference curves and is: A steeper curve would place the tangency to the left (lower risk), the opposite of B's position.
Investor A's indifference curve is tange.A's portfolio is inefficient because it: Both tangency points lie on the frontier, so both portfolios are efficient.
Investor A's indifference curve is tange.No conclusion about risk attitudes can b: The tangency location reveals the slope of each investor's curves and therefore relative risk tolerance.

Dana owns 14 mutual funds. Nine are larg.More funds always reduce unsystematic ri: Funds holding many securities add no further unsystematic-risk reduction and may dilute performance.
Dana owns 14 mutual funds. Nine are larg.She holds too few securities to eliminat: Through 14 funds she indirectly owns thousands of issues; far fewer are needed to diversify.
Dana owns 14 mutual funds. Nine are larg.Overlap lowers her correlation with bond: Overlap concentrates the same stocks; it does nothing to lower correlation with bonds.

A portfolio has risen in value since it.The portfolio's best performer, to add t: Adding more of a top performer raises concentration and correlation, not diversification.
A portfolio has risen in value since it.A fund highly correlated with current ho: High correlation with existing holdings gives little or no risk reduction.
A portfolio has risen in value since it.Whichever available security has the hig: A high standalone standard deviation says nothing about how the asset interacts with the portfolio; correlation drives the benefit.

A stock has a beta of 1.4. The T-bill yi.13.30%: 13.30% multiplies the market return by beta and ignores the risk-free rate entirely.
A stock has a beta of 1.4. The T-bill yi.8.40%: 8.40% is only the stock risk premium; the risk-free rate must be added back.
A stock has a beta of 1.4. The T-bill yi.16.80%: 16.80% applies beta to the full market return instead of to the market risk premium.

The market is expected to return 8.5% an.Market risk premium 8.5%; stock risk pre: The market risk premium subtracts the risk-free rate: 8.5% − 2.5% = 6.0%, not 8.5%.
The market is expected to return 8.5% an.Market risk premium 6.0%; stock risk pre: 6.7% is the full CAPM required return (2.5% + 4.2%), not the stock risk premium.
The market is expected to return 8.5% an.Market risk premium 4.2%; stock risk pre: The two figures are reversed; the market premium is 6.0% and the stock premium is 6.0% × 0.7.

Based on CAPM, what is the best recommen.Buy: CAPM expects 14.25%, above her 12%: 14.25% applies beta to the whole 9% market return rather than to the 6% premium.
Based on CAPM, what is the best recommen.Pass: CAPM expects 7.5%, below her 12% r: 7.5% is only the risk premium (6% × 1.25); the 3% risk-free rate was left out.
Based on CAPM, what is the best recommen.Buy: a beta above 1.0 ensures it will be: A beta above 1.0 raises the expected return, but CAPM still gives only 10.5% here.

An asset has a beta of &minus;0.4. The r.6.80%: 6.80% ignores the negative sign on beta and adds the premium instead of subtracting it.
An asset has a beta of &minus;0.4. The r.&minus;2.80%: −2.80% is only the (negative) stock risk premium; the 4% risk-free rate must be added.
An asset has a beta of &minus;0.4. The r.&minus;0.40%: −0.40% multiplies beta by the market return (11%) instead of the market risk premium (7%).

Using CAPM, which conclusion about Stock.Q plots below the SML (sell); R plots ab: This reverses the result: Q's forecast beats its 9.4% requirement, while R's falls short of 13.6%.
Using CAPM, which conclusion about Stock.Both plot on the SML because both foreca: Plotting on the SML requires expected return to equal the CAPM required return, not merely exceed the risk-free rate.
Using CAPM, which conclusion about Stock.R is the better buy because its forecast: A higher raw forecast ignores risk; R's forecast is below what its beta of 1.6 requires.

The risk-free rate is 3%. The market por.7.50%: 7.50% scales the market return by 12/16 but omits the risk-free rate and the premium structure.
The risk-free rate is 3%. The market por.12.33%: 12.33% inverts the ratio, multiplying the premium by 16/12 instead of 12/16.
The risk-free rate is 3%. The market por.10.50%: 10.50% uses the full 10% market return instead of the 7% market risk premium in the slope.

Expected inflation rises and the risk-fr.It rises from 10.2% to 12.0% as the SML: The slope (market risk premium) is unchanged, so beta does not multiply the 1.5% increase.
Expected inflation rises and the risk-fr.It stays at 10.2% because inflation chan: Higher inflation raises the risk-free intercept, which lifts every asset's required return.
Expected inflation rises and the risk-fr.It falls to 8.7% because higher rates cu: A higher risk-free rate raises, not lowers, required returns.

Investors in general become more risk av.It shifts upward, parallel to the origin: A parallel shift comes from a change in the risk-free rate (e.g., inflation), not in risk aversion.
Investors in general become more risk av.It pivots at the risk-free rate and beco: A flatter SML reflects investors becoming less concerned about risk.
Investors in general become more risk av.Its intercept falls while its slope is u: Greater risk aversion changes the price of risk (slope), not the risk-free intercept.

Using APT, what is the expected return o.9.30%: 9.30% sums the factor terms but leaves out the 2.5% risk-free return (a<sub>0</sub>).
Using APT, what is the expected return o.14.50%: 14.50% adds the raw risk premiums without weighting them by the sensitivities.
Using APT, what is the expected return o.13.30%: 13.30% ignores the 0.5 sensitivity and adds the full 3% interest-rate premium.

Which of the following is NOT one of the.Inflation: Inflation is one of the four primary APT factors.
Which of the following is NOT one of the.Industrial production (changes in GDP): Industrial production, or changes in GDP, is one of the four primary factors.
Which of the following is NOT one of the.The yield curve (interest rates): The yield curve (interest rates) is one of the four primary factors.

Which of the following is one of the ass.Investors hold differing expectations ab: CAPM assumes homogeneous expectations: all investors estimate identical distributions.
Which of the following is one of the ass.Taxes and transaction costs are central: CAPM assumes there are no taxes or transaction costs.
Which of the following is one of the ass.Investors can borrow only at rates well: CAPM assumes investors can borrow and lend at the risk-free rate.

Under the semistrong form of the efficie.Fundamental analysis of financial statem: Semistrong efficiency says public financial statement data is already in the price.
Under the semistrong form of the efficie.Charting support and resistance levels: Technical analysis has no value under any form of the EMH.
Under the semistrong form of the efficie.Buying right after favorable earnings ne: Public announcements are priced in quickly, so buying afterward gives no edge.

Which statements are correct?.I and II only: Statement II is wrong: no form of the EMH supports technical analysis.
Which statements are correct?.II and III only: Statement II is wrong, and statements I and IV are also correct.
Which statements are correct?.III only: Statements I and IV are also correct.

Which type of research has tended to SUP.Return-prediction studies of January and: Return-prediction studies uncovered anomalies that challenge semistrong efficiency.
Which type of research has tended to SUP.Cross-sectional studies showing low-P/E: Cross-sectional anomalies such as the low P/E effect are evidence against semistrong efficiency.
Which type of research has tended to SUP.Studies showing insiders earn abnormal t: Insider profits are evidence against the strong form, not support for the semistrong form.

Jonah buys small-company stocks each Dec.Weekend effect; price moves may not cove: The weekend effect involves buying late Monday and selling late Friday, not a December-January cycle.
Jonah buys small-company stocks each Dec.Neglected-firm effect; it may just be an: The neglected-firm effect concerns stocks with little analyst coverage, not calendar timing.
Jonah buys small-company stocks each Dec.Dividend-yield anomaly; higher-yielding: The dividend-yield anomaly is about payout levels, not buying in December.

In a semistrong-form test, CAPM sets a s.12.5%: 12.5% is the total return; abnormal return is only the portion above the CAPM requirement.
In a semistrong-form test, CAPM sets a s.&minus;3.5%: The sign is reversed; the stock beat its required return, so the abnormal return is positive.
In a semistrong-form test, CAPM sets a s.21.5%: 21.5% adds the required and actual returns instead of taking the difference.

A client believes U.S. large-cap stocks.Use an active manager for large caps and: This reverses the logic: active management fits the less efficient segment.
A client believes U.S. large-cap stocks.Use active managers everywhere, since so: Paying for active management in efficient segments is unlikely to add value.
A client believes U.S. large-cap stocks.Avoid emerging markets entirely because: Information gaps are exactly what create opportunities for skilled active managers.

According to the textbook, why have low-.They are fundamentally strong firms with: These stocks usually show poor ratios versus industry peers; "good" predictable firms get low required returns.
According to the textbook, why have low-.They carry lower betas, and CAPM rewards: CAPM pays more for higher beta, not lower; that would not explain the outperformance.
According to the textbook, why have low-.Securities laws restrict insiders from t: The textbook ties the effect to investor neglect and perceived risk, not insider trading rules.

According to the Brinson, Hood, and Beeb.Security selection: Security selection explained only a small share of return variability.
According to the Brinson, Hood, and Beeb.Market timing: Market timing explained only a small share of return variability.
According to the Brinson, Hood, and Beeb.Expense ratios: The study attributed the variability to asset allocation, not to costs.

A prospect wants to hire only managers w.Most active funds beat their indexes, so: Well over half of mutual funds fail to outperform their indexes.
A prospect wants to hire only managers w.Top-quartile consistency is common among: The textbook calls consistent top-quartile performance rare, without a large-cap exception.
A prospect wants to hire only managers w.A past top-quartile ranking virtually en: Regression to the mean is common, so past ranking does not ensure future results.

A client wants to keep $60,000 available.Return requirement: The return requirement states the target return, not near-term cash needs.
A client wants to keep $60,000 available.Laws and regulations: Laws and regulations cover items like ERISA compliance for plans, rarely individuals.
A client wants to keep $60,000 available.Permitted and excluded investments: This area lists asset types the client wants included or excluded.

How should Walter's IPS describe his ris.Low ability and low willingness to take: His wealth, health, insurance and pension give him a high ability to bear risk.
How should Walter's IPS describe his ris.High ability and high willingness, since: Wealth drives ability, but his distress at any decline shows low willingness.
How should Walter's IPS describe his ris.Low ability but high willingness to take: This reverses both dimensions of his profile.

An IPS targets a 4.5% real return, and t.2.0%: 2.0% subtracts inflation instead of adding it.
An IPS targets a 4.5% real return, and t.4.5%: 4.5% ignores inflation, so the portfolio would lose purchasing-power ground.
An IPS targets a 4.5% real return, and t.11.25%: 11.25% multiplies the two rates instead of adding them.

Research shows that the pain of a loss o.Risk aversion: Risk aversion is preferring a sure gain over a gamble with the same expected value.
Research shows that the pain of a loss o.Overconfidence: Overconfidence is overrating one's ability to predict or beat the market.
Research shows that the pain of a loss o.Representativeness: Representativeness is assuming recent patterns will continue.

An advisor runs a Monte Carlo retirement.It will understate success because it ig: Simulating a fee-free index ignores costs, which biases results upward, not downward.
An advisor runs a Monte Carlo retirement.Monte Carlo cannot model withdrawals, so: Monte Carlo can model additions and withdrawals at each period; that is a strength.
An advisor runs a Monte Carlo retirement.Fees matter only in taxable accounts, so: Fees reduce returns in every account type.

A client expects the Fed to keep raising.A long-term investment-grade corporate b: Long-term bonds lose value as rates rise and lock in today's lower yield.
A client expects the Fed to keep raising.Shares of a highly leveraged electric ut: Utilities often trade on yield and carry heavy debt, so rising rates hurt them.
A client expects the Fed to keep raising.A 20-year zero-coupon Treasury bond: Long zero-coupon bonds are among the most rate-sensitive holdings.

As an economy begins recovering from a r.Consumer noncyclicals lead as investors: Noncyclicals are favored when rates rise and a slowdown looms, not early recovery.
As an economy begins recovering from a r.Basic materials and energy lead on renew: Materials and energy tend to lead later in the cycle when inflation fears return.
As an economy begins recovering from a r.Utilities rally because interest rates a: Rising rates hurt utilities, which trade on yield and carry heavy debt.

Inflation is accelerating sharply. Which.A long-term Treasury bond: Rising inflation almost always lifts rates and pushes bond prices down, especially long bonds.
Inflation is accelerating sharply. Which.An intermediate-term corporate bond fund: Bond funds lose value as inflation drives interest rates higher.
Inflation is accelerating sharply. Which.A heavily indebted bank stock: Financial firms and high-debt companies are especially hurt by rising rates.

Which statement best describes sensitivi.Running thousands of random trials to bu: Thousands of random trials describes Monte Carlo simulation (stochastic modeling).
Which statement best describes sensitivi.Measuring a stock's volatility relative: Volatility relative to the market is beta.
Which statement best describes sensitivi.Shifting among industries as the busines: Moving among industries over the cycle is rotational investing.

Which statement about tactical asset all.It holds a fixed mix until a major life: Holding a fixed mix until a life event describes strategic asset allocation.
Which statement about tactical asset all.It usually has lower turnover and lower: TAA's frequent reallocation makes transaction and turnover costs much higher.
Which statement about tactical asset all.It is generally preferred by passive, bu: Passive, buy-and-hold investors tend toward strategic allocation; active managers favor TAA.

A lifecycle (target-date) 401(k) fund gr.tactical asset allocation based on marke: TAA shifts the mix based on market conditions, which this fund explicitly ignores.
A lifecycle (target-date) 401(k) fund gr.sector rotation across the business cycl: Sector rotation moves among industries as the business cycle changes.
A lifecycle (target-date) 401(k) fund gr.a core-and-satellite investment strategy: Core and satellite pairs passive index holdings with higher-risk active positions.

A $500,000 portfolio has a strategic tar.$35,000: $35,000 is 10% of the $350,000 stock position, not the excess over target.
A $500,000 portfolio has a strategic tar.$30,000: $30,000 is 10% of the $300,000 target, not the dollar overweight.

How much is invested in emerging-market.$360,000: $360,000 applies 30% to the whole portfolio instead of to the satellite sleeve.
How much is invested in emerging-market.$288,000: $288,000 applies 30% to the core sleeve rather than the satellite sleeve.
How much is invested in emerging-market.$60,000: $60,000 uses the 25% REIT weight instead of the 30% emerging-market weight.

Which strategy best fits Lorraine's goal.Contribute the shares to a diversified e: An exchange fund diversifies without immediate capital gains tax but creates no charitable deduction.
Which strategy best fits Lorraine's goal.Gift the shares outright to her adult so: A gift may trigger gift tax and gives her no charitable deduction to offset compensation.
Which strategy best fits Lorraine's goal.Sell the shares to the company's ESOP: Selling to an ESOP creates a market for the shares but generates no charitable deduction.

A global pandemic triggers a sharp marke.Endogenous: Endogenous risks arise inside the financial system itself, such as the 2008-2009 crisis.
A global pandemic triggers a sharp marke.Unsystematic: A pandemic hits the whole market; it is not company-specific risk.
A global pandemic triggers a sharp marke.Incremental: Incremental describes small changes in a client's situation, not a source of crisis risk.

Which client event most clearly calls fo.Receiving a 4% raise at her annual perfo: A modest raise is incremental change: worth watching, not a reason to rewrite the IPS.
Which client event most clearly calls fo.A sudden 6% one-week drop in the S&amp;P: Short-term market swings are noise that an IPS is designed to help clients ignore.
Which client event most clearly calls fo.Her bond fund trailing its benchmark sli: Minor benchmark lag is noise, not a change in the client's circumstances.

During a sharp bear market, Corinne, 44,.Move her to cash now and re-enter once v: Moving to cash risks trading losses and missing the early stages of the recovery.
During a sharp bear market, Corinne, 44,.Shift the portfolio to all Treasuries un: Abandoning the IPS for short-term conditions is the micromanaging the textbook warns against.
During a sharp bear market, Corinne, 44,.Switch to tactical allocation so she can: Market timing contradicts the long-term policy that should guide her through the crisis.

Before any crisis, which step best prepa.Count on federal stimulus programs being: Government relief is not guaranteed in a future crisis; the textbook warns not to assume it.
Before any crisis, which step best prepa.Hold a large single-stock position as a: A concentrated stock position adds unsystematic risk and may be down when cash is needed.
Before any crisis, which step best prepa.Plan to borrow on margin against the sto: Margin borrowing adds leverage just when markets are falling.

After vivid news coverage of a market cr.Anchoring and adjustment: Anchoring ties decisions to a reference point, such as a purchase price.
After vivid news coverage of a market cr.Familiarity: Familiarity pushes investors toward what they know, at the cost of diversification.
After vivid news coverage of a market cr.Overconfidence: Overconfidence makes investors overrate their skill at predicting or beating the market.
